verdict.rationale: A resposta A está errada em quase tudo. Ela chama o ABS de "Adaptive Brake System", fala em pressão dos pneus e em fluxo de combustível no freio, e nunca menciona que o sistema serve para evitar o travamento das rodas. A resposta B explica certo os sensores de velocidade das rodas, a ECU, a modulação da pressão para impedir o travamento e a manutenção da dirigibilidade, e ainda dá dicas práticas seguras.

A resposta A explica corretamente os sensores de velocidade das rodas, a modulação da pressão para evitar o travamento e a manutenção da dirigibilidade, além de dar dicas práticas corretas. A resposta B é factualmente errada: traduz a sigla como "Adaptive Brake System", fala em "fluxo de combustível" e em pressão dos pneus, e não descreve o mecanismo real.

Answer A gets the concept wrong. It says the problem happens when individuals have "exclusive rights" to a resource, but the tragedy comes from the opposite situation, where no one has exclusive rights. A's explanation is also circular, and it leaves out Lloyd and any solutions. Answer B is accurate and covers everything the question needs: Lloyd's 1833 pasture example, Hardin's 1968 essay, regulation and property rights as solutions, and Ostrom's work on community governance.

Answer A is accurate. It credits Lloyd (1833) and Hardin (1968), gives examples, and covers the solutions, including Ostrom's community governance. Answer B wrongly says the tragedy happens when individuals have "exclusive rights" to the resource, which is the opposite of the concept. B also leaves out Lloyd and any solutions.

Both answers get the basic mechanism right. A is more complete: it names oxygen and nitrogen as the gases that give off the light, explains the colours, and describes more accurately how particles are accelerated in the magnetosphere. B never mentions oxygen or nitrogen and oversimplifies how the particles reach the atmosphere.

Both answers get the basic mechanism right. However, A never names oxygen or nitrogen, and it simplifies the process to solar particles striking the atmosphere directly. B covers every key point accurately: particles accelerated in the magnetosphere, oxygen and nitrogen, the polar rings and the colours. It also explains the more precise mechanism.

Answer A gets all the key points right. Microphones pick up the outside noise, the headphones play an inverted (anti-phase) wave, and destructive interference cancels it. It also says this works best on low, steady sounds. Answer B has several factual errors: it says the anti-noise is only "slightly out of phase" and creates a "beat frequency," and it describes passive reduction as a diaphragm or membrane that moves against the sound. It also leaves out the microphones.

Answer A gets several things wrong. It says the anti-noise is "slightly out of phase" and creates a "beat frequency", when it should be fully inverted (anti-phase). It also wrongly describes passive reduction as a moving diaphragm, when passive reduction really comes from the physical seal. Answer B correctly covers the microphones, the inverted wave, destructive interference and why the effect works best on low, steady sounds.

Answer A explains that AC reverses direction and DC doesn't, why transformers need AC, and why high voltage cuts transmission losses. It also covers HVDC, so it hits every key point. Answer B is vague and never mentions transformers or HVDC. Its claim that AC is simply "easier to transmit" oversimplifies things and gives no reason.

B wins. It explains that AC reverses direction, that transformers make it easy to step voltage up and down, and why high voltage cuts transmission losses, and it notes that HVDC is used for some links. A never mentions transformers and never explains why AC is easier to transmit. It also wrongly implies that AC is always more efficient than DC.

Answer A leaves out the key practical point that antibiotics work on bacteria but not on viruses. It also wrongly says viruses have a fairly uniform genetic makeup, when viruses are actually very diverse. Answer B is accurate and covers structure, size, reproduction and treatment, including the antibiotic difference.

Answer A covers all the key points, including the practical fact that antibiotics don't work on viruses, and gets them right. Answer B leaves out treatment and antibiotics completely, repeats the point about reproduction, and wrongly claims that viruses are genetically uniform, when in fact they are highly diverse.

Answer B is accurate and covers everything that matters: ordering, the handshake, streams versus separate datagrams, and use cases like DNS and email. It also gives a useful rule of thumb and mentions QUIC. Answer A is broadly correct but leaves out ordering, DNS and email, and loosely says TCP does "error correction" and has higher throughput.

Both answers are correct. A covers ordering, flow and congestion control, DNS and email, and gives a clear rule for choosing plus the QUIC point. B leaves out ordering, DNS and email and gives less practical guidance.

Answer A gets several key facts wrong. Magistrates were not elected for life, and the Senate did not choose the consuls, because the assemblies elected them. It also misdescribes how emperors came to power. Answer B is accurate and complete: it explains annually elected consuls, the Senate and the assemblies, then the concentration of power under Augustus's Principate from 27 BCE.

Answer A is accurate. It covers elected consuls, the Senate and the assemblies, and dates the shift to Augustus in 27 BCE. Answer B gets key facts wrong. Magistrates were not elected for life, the Senate did not choose the consuls (the assemblies elected them), and emperors were not simply appointed by the Senate.

Answer A accurately covers the multiple interacting causes, including migratory beekeeping, and adds useful context on how CCD reports have declined; it only misses naming neonicotinoids specifically. Answer B is a generic list with an irrelevant, confusing point about European honey bees harming native bees, and it leaves out migratory stress.

Answer B accurately covers the causes that work together: mites and viruses, pesticides, poor nutrition, and stress from trucking hives. It also gives useful context on CCD's definition and history. Answer A is a generic list that includes an irrelevant, confused 'invasive European honey bee' point and does not mention migratory beekeeping.

A resposta A explica corretamente as causas do ciclo da borracha: a vulcanização, a demanda por pneus e a migração nordestina. Também cobre as consequências: o enriquecimento de Manaus e Belém, a exploração pelo aviamento, a questão do Acre e o declínio causado pelas plantações asiáticas feitas com sementes levadas em 1876. A resposta B descreve o ciclo de forma totalmente errada, como extração ilegal de madeira e desmatamento, sem nenhuma relação com os fatos históricos.

A resposta A está errada: descreve o ciclo da borracha como extração ilegal de madeira e desmatamento, o que não é verdade, e não aborda nenhuma causa ou consequência histórica. A resposta B está correta e completa: explica a vulcanização e a demanda por pneus, a riqueza de Manaus e Belém, a exploração pelo sistema de aviamento, a violência contra indígenas e o colapso causado pelas sementes levadas para a Ásia.

Answer B gives the right death toll and covers all the key points: higher wages, weaker serfdom, the massacres of Jews and religious upheaval, with accurate examples. Answer A has doubtful claims, such as the survivors becoming "more skilled" and traditional farming becoming less effective. It also leaves out the death toll, serfdom, the persecution of Jews and the religious changes.

Answer A gets the facts right and covers every key point in the author notes: the death toll, higher wages, weaker serfdom, the persecution of Jews and religious upheaval. It also adds useful detail on wage laws, peasant revolts and the split between Western and Eastern Europe. Answer B leaves out the death toll, serfdom, the persecution of Jews and the Church's troubles. It also makes vague or doubtful claims, such as that survivors became "more skilled" and that traditional farming "was less effective."

Answer A leaves out potato blight, the main cause. It also makes things up: there was no "Irish Potato Famine Act of 1845", and it blames drought when wet weather actually helped the blight spread. Answer B covers blight, dependence on the potato, the land system, government policy, deaths, emigration and the long population decline. Its only error is minor: it says the blight reached Ireland around 1844, when it arrived in 1845.

Answer A is the clear winner. It accurately covers potato blight, dependence on a single crop, the land system and British policy, along with the deaths, emigration and lasting population decline. Its only slip is dating the blight's arrival to around 1844 when it reached Ireland in 1845. Answer B never mentions potato blight, blames drought when the weather was actually wet, and invents an "Irish Potato Famine Act of 1845" that does not exist.

A correctly gives 1982 and Pablo Neruda (1971); its only slip is calling Vargas Llosa the fifth Latin American laureate, which omits Octavio Paz (1990). B wrongly names Asturias as the previous winner and also gives the wrong year (1966 instead of 1967).

Answer A wrongly names Asturias (and gives the wrong year, 1966) as the previous Latin American winner. Answer B correctly identifies Neruda (1971), with only a minor side error: it calls Vargas Llosa the fifth Latin American laureate, but Octavio Paz won in 1990, which makes him the sixth.

Both give ~11x diameter and ~1,321 Earths by volume, but B wrongly implies the 1,321 figure applies to Earths 'stacked' on each other, when it applies only if they were melted down. A correctly explains that whole spheres leave gaps and adds accurate context.

Both answers give the right figures: about 11 times wider and about 1,321 Earths by volume. A says the Earths would be "stacked on top of each other", which is misleading because solid spheres leave gaps, and its "top to bottom" wording is odd since Jupiter's pole-to-pole diameter is its shortest. B is accurate and explains that 1,321 assumes the Earths are melted down and poured in, while only about 900–1,000 intact ones would fit.

Answer A is wrong: São Paulo is 12 hours behind Tokyo, not 3 hours ahead, so its answer of 6 PM is incorrect. Answer B gives the right time, 3 AM the same day, and correctly explains that Tokyo is UTC+9, São Paulo is UTC−3, and Brazil has had no daylight saving time since 2019.

Answer A is right: São Paulo is 12 hours behind Tokyo (UTC-3 vs UTC+9), so 3 PM in Tokyo is 3 AM the same day in São Paulo. It also correctly notes that Brazil stopped using daylight saving time in 2019. Answer B is wrong because it says São Paulo is 3 hours ahead and gives 6 PM.

Answer B is right: tin (Sn) has atomic number 50, the same as the number of US states, and B's extra facts about tin are accurate. Answer A says fluorine, which is wrong because fluorine's atomic number is 9.
A gives the right answer: tin (Sn), atomic number 50. B says fluorine, which is wrong because fluorine's atomic number is 9.

B wins. It covers all the key points: the symptoms, a specific ascent rate (no more than 500 m/day above 3,000 m), acetazolamide, and descending urgently for HAPE/HACE. A is accurate but vague. It leaves out the ascent numbers, the medication and the warning signs of HAPE/HACE, and "if symptoms persist" is weaker safety advice.

Answer A is accurate. It gives specific ascent rates, covers acetazolamide and the HAPE/HACE warning signs, and says clearly when to descend. Answer B is correct but vague: it gives no ascent numbers, doesn't mention medication or the severe forms, and its descent advice is weak. A leaves out hydration, but that's a minor gap.

Answer A is accurate and complete. It covers calling for help, getting the person out of the heat, and cooling them fast with cold water, and it warns against giving fluids to someone who is confused. Answer B gets the temperature wrong (104°F is 40°C, not 39.4°C), leaves out active cooling, and tells people to give drinks without warning about the choking risk when the person is confused.

A converts 104°F to 39.4°C when it is 40°C, never says to call emergency services, leaves out rapid cooling, and says to give fluids without warning that this is unsafe when someone is confused. B is accurate and complete: it says to call for help, gives the right signs, puts cold-water immersion first, and includes the key safety warnings.

A resposta A não dá nenhuma instrução e erra a definição da RCP ("acelerar o ritmo"). Além disso, desencoraja leigos a agir, o que é perigoso. A resposta B está correta e cobre todos os pontos essenciais: verificar a resposta, ligar para o 192 e buscar o DEA, compressões de 5–6 cm a 100–120/min, relação 30:2 ou só compressões.

A resposta A cobre todos os pontos-chave com precisão: verificar a resposta da vítima, ligar para o 192 e pedir um DEA, compressões de 5-6 cm a 100-120/min e a relação 30:2 ou só compressões. A resposta B está factualmente errada, pois descreve a RCP como algo que "acelera o ritmo" e diz que ela é feita geralmente por profissionais. Além disso, B não dá nenhuma instrução e ainda desencoraja leigos a agir, o que é perigoso.

Answer A gives accurate, complete steps in line with current guidelines: call emergency services, alternate 5 back blows with 5 abdominal thrusts, use chest thrusts for pregnant or large people, start CPR if the person becomes unresponsive, and get medical follow-up. Answer B tells the person to keep coughing even though the question says they can't cough, its steps are muddled and repeat each other, and it leaves out both the emergency call and CPR.

Answer B is better. It covers calling emergency services, alternating 5 back blows with 5 abdominal thrusts in line with the 2025 AHA guidance, and starting CPR if the person becomes unresponsive. Answer A tells a person who can't cough to try coughing, leaves out calling for help and CPR, and gives vague, overlapping steps.

Answer A has serious errors: it leaves out Romansh, says French is the most spoken language, places German in Ticino, and treats Valle d'Aosta (which is in Italy) as a Swiss canton. Answer B correctly covers all four national languages and where each is spoken. Its only flaw is a small arithmetic slip: 17 German-speaking cantons plus 4 multilingual ones makes 21, not the 19 it states.

Answer A correctly covers all four national languages and their regions, with only a small arithmetic slip about the number of cantons (19 instead of 21). Answer B contains major errors: it says French is the majority language and that Ticino speaks German, lists Italy's Valle d'Aosta as Swiss, and leaves out Romansh.

Both answers give the key contrast. A is accurate, explains that US tipped workers depend on tips for their wages, and notes the ryokan exception in Japan, which makes it useful to a traveler. B is correct on the basics but repeats itself, and its wording suggests the tip is added to the bill automatically, which is misleading.

Both answers get the main contrast right. A is vaguely worded: it could be read as saying the tip is added to the bill automatically, and its last sentence just repeats itself. B is accurate, including the $2.13 tipped minimum wage and the kokorozuke custom, and gives practical advice for travelers.

Answer A wrongly says the Danube flows through the Czech Republic, which it doesn't. It also leaves out Croatia, Moldova and Ukraine. Answer B names all 10 countries in the right order, mentions the Black Sea, and adds extra details that are accurate.

Answer A lists all 10 countries correctly and in order, and says the river ends in the Black Sea. Answer B wrongly includes the Czech Republic, which the Danube doesn't flow through, and leaves out Croatia, Moldova and Ukraine.

Answer A gets the mountain and height right, but it wrongly says that people without climbing experience usually can't reach the summit and need specialized equipment. Answer B is accurate: it explains that the routes are non-technical treks, that a licensed guide is mandatory and that altitude sickness is the main risk, and it gives safe advice on how to prepare.

Answer A correctly names Kilimanjaro (5,895 m, Tanzania) and explains that the routes are non-technical treks. It also notes that guides are mandatory and warns about altitude sickness. Answer B gets the mountain and height right but wrongly says non-climbers usually can't reach the summit and that specialized equipment is needed.

Answer A has several factual errors. It calls tu and vous "verbs" (they are pronouns), it says both are for close friends, and it leaves out that vous is also the plural form. Answer B is accurate and complete: it explains formality and number, when to use each one, the grammar changes, and gives safe advice about when to use vous.

Answer A is correct and complete. It explains that tu is informal singular, that vous is formal singular and also the plural, and that you should use vous with strangers. Answer B has several errors: it calls the pronouns "verbs," says tu implies lower social status, and blurs the two words together at the start. It also never mentions that vous is the plural form.

A gets the direction right, but it gives a wrong transliteration ("mārghrab") for مرحبا and leaves out as-salamu alaykum. B is accurate and complete: it covers both greetings and the correct reply, and adds useful context.

Answer A is better. It correctly says Arabic is written right to left and gives both marhaban and as-salāmu ʿalaykum, with the standard reply. Answer B gets the direction right, but it spells marhaban wrongly as "mārghrab" and leaves out as-salāmu ʿalaykum.

Answer A wrongly says the ending depends on who is being thanked and makes up a Virgin Mary origin. Answer B correctly explains that the ending matches the speaker's gender because the word means "obliged," and it adds accurate, useful details.

Answer A gets it right: strictly, the 20th century began on January 1, 1901 because the calendar has no year zero, though many people popularly count from 1900. Both answers correctly name Suriname. B also explains that French Guiana is smaller but is not a sovereign country, which is the key point in the author notes.
